source: Lugoloobi, Foster, Bankes, Russell (2026) LLMs Encode Their Failures: Predicting Success from Pre-Generation Activations (COLM 2026)
finding: Linear probes on pre-generation hidden states predict a model's own success rate better than question length. The signal gets weaker as the model reasons more.
numbers: E2H-AMC (4k problems). Spearman probe vs model success rate: Qwen2.5-Math 1.5B .64, 7B .64; GPT-OSS-20B low .58, medium .50, high .40. Length baseline .15 to .30. Human IRT difficulty probe .83 to .87 for all. MLP probe at GPT-OSS high: .11.
limits: Open-weight models only (GPT-OSS-20B, Qwen2.5, R1-distill-7B). Needs hidden-state access. K=5 rollouts for GPT-OSS, K=50 for Qwen.
agent_relevance: An internal difficulty signal beats a length proxy at the item level, but is not available to an API-only scaffold. Human-like difficulty is easy to read out, model-specific difficulty is not.

source: Lugoloobi et al. (2026) LLMs Encode Their Failures, Table 2 and routing section
finding: Binary success (greedy, Maj@5) is predictable from pre-generation states; probe quality degrades with test-time compute. Routing on the probe cuts cost.
numbers: AUROC > .7 for most settings, several > .8; Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B greedy .84 vs length .61. GPT-OSS-20B Maj@5 AUROC .78 to .64 as reasoning goes low to high while accuracy rose 86.6% to 92.0%. Router matches best single model (GPT-OSS-20B-high, 92%) at about 70% lower cost on MATH.
limits: Single group; probes trained per model; cost accounting ignores probe training. Table rows partly garbled in text extraction.
agent_relevance: Closes part of GAP 8: a model-internal signal tracks difficulty better than token count, and it supports routing by difficulty (cheap vs expensive reasoning). A text-only agent can only use proxies.

source: Cencerrado, Pacchiardi et al. (2026) No Answer Needed: Predicting LLM Answer Accuracy from Question-Only Linear Probes (ICLR 2026 workshop)
finding: A difference-of-means direction read before generation predicts correctness in distribution and out of distribution for knowledge questions, and beats verbalised predicted confidence. It falters on math reasoning.
numbers: Three open model families, 7B to 70B. Abstract: probe outperforms black-box baselines and verbalised confidence; generalisation falters on math. One reported probe row AUROC .760 to .875 depending on model and dataset, .587 to .678 on the weak ones.
limits: Trivia-trained probe; math is exactly where it fails; verbalised-confidence prompt is one prompt.
agent_relevance: A verbalised pre-solve estimate is a weak instrument compared with probes, and on reasoning tasks nothing cheap generalises. Expect low value from a self-rated difficulty step.

source: Kale (2026) Future Confidence Distillation in Large Language Models (arXiv 2607.07626)
finding: Pre-solution verbal confidence (feeling of knowing) is worse calibrated and less discriminative than post-solution confidence; hidden-state probes recover more than the models say.
numbers: Frontier models GPT-5.4 and Claude Sonnet 4.6, verbal pre vs post AUROC (mean of 3 seeds): factual .57/.61 and .66/.70; logic .68/.69 and .77/.70; math .72/.75 and .50/.79 (row-to-model mapping partly ambiguous in text extraction). Pre ECE on math up to .38. Probes gain .09 to .15 AUROC on some domains.
limits: Confidence about correctness, not a 1 to 9 difficulty or effort rating. Two frontier models only.
agent_relevance: Closest direct data for GAP 1: a rating given before solving is near chance in some model and domain cells (.50 to .57) and clearly above chance in others (.72 to .77). Verify per model before relying on it.

source: Feng, Kempe et al. (2025) What Characterizes Effective Reasoning? Revisiting Length, Review, and Structure of CoT (Meta)
finding: Within the same question, shorter chains of thought go with higher accuracy across ten reasoning models. A structural count, the failed-step fraction, predicts correctness better than length.
numbers: 16 CoTs per question, HARP and GPQA-Diamond; conditional (question-fixed-effect) correlation plus Bayesian GLMM agree in sign. Length negative for most models. Selecting by FSF at test time gives up to 10% gain on AIME; removing failed branches raises accuracy (up to 12% on math in one setting).
limits: Correlational for length; filtered out questions where all 16 samples agree; Claude 3.7 shows the opposite sign for review ratio. Some numbers in figures only.
agent_relevance: Directly answers GAP 3: yes, longer-thinking items fail more, even within item. But it is the failed-branch share, not raw length, that carries the signal. Log abandoned branches, not just tokens.

source: Ballon, Algaba, Ginis (2026) The relationship between reasoning and performance in LLMs: o3 (mini) thinks harder, not longer (Scientific Reports 16:20896)
finding: Accuracy falls as reasoning chains get longer for o1-mini and o3-mini, even controlling for difficulty tier and domain. The drop is smaller in stronger models.
numbers: Omni-MATH. Average marginal effect of +1000 reasoning tokens on P(correct): -3.16% o1-mini, -1.96% o3-mini (m), -0.81% o3-mini (h). o3-mini (m) uses fewer tokens than o1-mini on 63% of jointly solved items. o3-mini (h) uses more than double the tokens of (m) for about +4% accuracy.
limits: Math only; OpenAI o-series only; logistic regression with tier and domain controls, not item fixed effects.
agent_relevance: Supports GAP 3 with difficulty controls: a token-count slope on error is real but shrinks with capability, so a token threshold must be calibrated per model.

source: Su, Healey, Nakov, Cardie (2025) Between Underthinking and Overthinking: reasoning length and correctness in LLMs
finding: Accuracy rises with length at first, then falls. Models overthink easy items and underthink hard ones, so they misjudge difficulty when setting length.
numbers: Abstract-level: length can be cut a lot by preferring shorter answers regardless of correctness while keeping acceptable accuracy.
limits: Only abstract and introduction read; per-model numbers not extracted.
agent_relevance: Tokens spent is a poor monotone load gauge; it follows difficulty only loosely. Fits claim K19, now with a full-text source.

source: Bamgbose et al. (2026) DNR Bench: Benchmarking Over-Reasoning in Reasoning LLMs (AAAI-26), Table 2
finding: An explicit instruction line raises accuracy of reasoning models on tricky or redundant prompts under a 1000-token cap, and cuts tokens, but does not fix over-reasoning.
numbers: 150 prompts, 5 categories; accuracy default / with instructions within 1000 tokens. Redundant (n=25): DeepSeek-R1 .00 / .76; Claude-3.7-Thinking .40 / 1.00; o3-mini-high .00 / .04; GPT-4o 1.00 / 1.00. Unanswerable (n=50): R1 .00 / .20; Claude .12 / .82; GPT-4o .42 / .98. Indifferent category: instructions hurt (Claude .80 / .04).
limits: Not a distractor-in-math test like GSM-IC; prompts are adversarial 'do not reason' items; judge is GPT-4o-mini (Pearson .455 vs manual labels on a validation set); small n per category.
agent_relevance: Partly closes GAP 2: at a matched 1000-token cap an instruction line gives large gains for some reasoning models and none for others (o3-mini-high). The instruction is cheap but model specific, and it can backfire.

source: Bamgbose et al. (2026) DNR Bench, token and budget-control results
finding: All models are less accurate in longer responses; reasoning models emit up to 70 times the tokens of GPT-4o; reasoning-budget settings do not cure it.
numbers: Up to 70x tokens vs GPT-4o by default; 2x to 20x with instructions. Budget control (Table 3): GPT-OSS-120B high on Math .16, Redundant .28, Unanswerable .12; GPT-OSS-20B medium .08 / .00 / .02. Gemini-2.5-Pro over 2000 tokens average, about 10x GPT-4o. DS-R1-Distill-14B produced over 27,000 tokens and repeated one block 120 times.
limits: Adversarial easy prompts; token count mixes reasoning and answer text.
agent_relevance: Supports GAP 3 and K10 (effort setting is a cap, not a dial for easy items). Cheap guard: an early-stop rule on repeated text.

source: Tran and Kiela (2026) Single-Agent LLMs Outperform Multi-Agent Systems on Multi-Hop Reasoning Under Equal Thinking Token Budgets
finding: With thinking tokens held equal, a single agent matches or beats five multi-agent designs on FRAMES and MuSiQue. Reported multi-agent gains are partly unaccounted compute and benchmark artifacts.
numbers: Three families (Qwen3-30B-A3B, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B, Gemini 2.5 Flash/Pro); budgets 100 to 10,000 thinking tokens; sequential, subtask-parallel, roles, debate, ensemble MAS. Sample cell: MuSiQue R1-70B at one budget SAS .418 vs Sequential .327. Light paraphrase lowered SAS (Gemini .331 to .326); deep paraphrase raised it (.331 to .358 at 1k).
limits: Multi-hop QA only, under review, API budget-control artifacts found (esp. Gemini 2.5). MAS can win when single-agent context use degrades or compute rises. Table header columns partly garbled in extraction.
agent_relevance: Closes GAP 7 for multi-hop QA: split-into-agents is not a free load reducer at equal tokens. Contradicts the unequal-budget wins in the earlier CLT multi-agent source (K17).

source: Minkley, Xu, Krell (2021) Analyzing Relationships Between Causal and Assessment Factors of Cognitive Load (Frontiers in Education 6:632907)
finding: Out of the lab, in a school biology project, heart rate variability related to self-reported effort but not mental load, and the ratings predicted task performance better than the heart measures.
numbers: N=309 high school students, three studies, chest-belt HRV. Regression on performance: mental load beta -.326 (p<.001), mental effort beta +.309 (p<.001), LF/HF beta .174 (p=.051), RMSSD beta -.084 (p=.344). Most significant correlations explain under 10% of variance (R2).
limits: Field-like (out-of-school lab day), not a classroom; one subject domain; performance on a test given there.
agent_relevance: GAP 5 evidence from the field side: physiology is the weak link; effort has the opposite sign from load. For an agent: effort spent and difficulty are different signals.

source: Zu, Munsell, Rebello (2021) Subjective Measure of Cognitive Load Depends on Participants' Content Knowledge Level (Frontiers in Education 6:647097)
finding: An eight-item three-load survey shows a three-factor structure only after learners gain knowledge; with low prior knowledge it shows two components. Ratings followed the manipulated load type in experiment 3.
numbers: Exp 1 N=45 card sort (13 interviewed); Exp 2 N=139 pre/post PCA: two components at low knowledge, three at higher knowledge; Exp 3 N=40 problems with different intrinsic and extraneous load.
limits: University physics students; a single survey instrument; small N in exp 3.
agent_relevance: Boundary condition for K02 and K03: the apparent two-factor model is partly a novice effect. A weak model may not separate intrinsic from extraneous load, which fits the LLM finding that small models fail at baseline.

source: Authors not extracted (2021) Measuring Cognitive Load: Are There More Valid Alternatives to Likert Rating Scales? (Frontiers in Education 6:702616)
finding: Four scale formats compared on the same problems: pictorial scales tracked performance better on simple problems, numeric scales on complex ones. The article also restates DeLeeuw and Mayer.
numbers: N=46 (39 women, mean age 22.4); 2 (complexity) x 4 (scale type) within subjects; complexity effect on difficulty F(1,45)=1306.63, p<.001, partial eta2=.97; accuracy .95 simple vs .51 complex on the 9-point scale; preferences 16 original, 14 VAS, 13 emoticons, 3 weights.
limits: Read through a page summary tool, last 8k characters unread; student sample; DeLeeuw and Mayer details are second-hand here (no N or correlations reported).
agent_relevance: The best rating format depends on task difficulty; the numeric 9-point scale is not dominated. Supports a single numeric rating for hard items only.

source: Hart and Staveland, NASA Task Load Index (TLX) v1.0 computerized manual (NASA Ames, via NTRS 20000021487)
finding: The manual describes the TLX design: six subscales, 15 pairwise comparisons giving weights 0 to 5, and why weights were kept. It reports no reliability coefficient.
numbers: Six subscales (mental, physical, temporal demand; performance, effort, frustration). Earlier 9-subscale bipolar scale was too long and partly redundant. One weight set reused across versions of a task added only slight sensitivity for the cost. Retrospective ratings correlated highly with online ratings in helicopter and supervisory-control simulations (no r given in text).
limits: This is the software manual, not the 1988 chapter. Test-retest or sensitivity statistics (GAP 4) remain unfound. OCR text is noisy.
agent_relevance: Weighting adds little: use a single raw effort or difficulty number and skip the 15-comparison step. The agent analogue is a one-line self-rating, not a six-scale form.

source: Skulmowski and Rey (2017) Measuring Cognitive Load in Embodied Learning Settings (Frontiers in Psychology 8:1191)
finding: Mini-review of embodied-learning studies: subjective scales usable if the wording fits, TLX mostly found no differences, dual-task measures are problematic, physiology needs mobile kit.
numbers: In two experiments by Skulmowski and Rey (2017) and two by Kaspar and Vennekoetter (2015), the TLX gave no significant difference for most subscales; effort was significant in one, physical demand in two. Paas mental-effort item: significant in some studies (Castro-Alonso 2015a; Wong 2015 exp 1), not in others (Ruiter 2015; Pouw 2016a).
limits: A 2017 review, not the 2020 paper named in the row; I could not find a 2020 Skulmowski and Rey paper on measurement. No effect sizes.
agent_relevance: Partly closes GAP 5: the 'did not hold outside the lab' claim is a mixed vote count, not a measured gap. Treat it as weakly supported.

source: DeLeeuw and Mayer (2008) via FORRT replication atlas and the Frontiers 702616 summary
finding: Atlas lists one replication of DeLeeuw and Mayer: Zu et al. (2020, J Educ Psychol), outcome successful (read from the abstract). The 702616 article states the original pattern: difficulty ratings relate to intrinsic load, effort ratings to germane load.
numbers: No sample sizes or correlations recovered. Original paper full text not retrievable (core.ac.uk 403; typeset.io returned HTML).
limits: Second-hand only. GAP 4 second half stays open.
agent_relevance: Keep the pattern as a hypothesis: difficulty rating tracks task demand, effort rating tracks invested resource; test both in the agent.

source: Search outcome, GAP 1 and GAP 6 (null result), 2026-11-20
finding: Searches for a paper testing a pre-solve 1 to 9 difficulty or effort rating against correctness and tokens in reasoning models found none. Searches for a CogniLoad replication on another benchmark found none.
numbers: Several web searches plus snippet scans; closest are d01, d03, d04 (probes and verbalised confidence).
limits: Absence in a narrow search is weak evidence; arXiv API and Semantic Scholar were rate limited (HTTP 429).
agent_relevance: GAP 1 and GAP 6 stay open; they are experiments to run in-house.
